name: Care Services
summary: Overnight respite care for dementia caregivers.
description:
What Is Night Respite?
Night Respite is an overnight respite option for caregivers of persons requiring mild to moderate assistance in their Activities of Daily Living (ADL) or persons living with dementia displaying sundowning behaviour. This service provides caregivers with the opportunity to take time off from night time caregiving duties.
How it Helps Caregivers
Night Respite engages persons in need living with dementia meaningfully providing support for their ADLs.
The service not only enable caregivers to take time off from caregiving duties to catch up on rest or fulfil other commitments. It also support caregivers in managing the sundowning issues of their loved ones.
Download the Night Respite brochure here.
What is Sundowning?
Sundowning is the worsening of behavioural difficulties towards the end of the day. Symptoms include restlessness, agitation, suspicious behaviour, disorientation, visual and auditory hallucinations, and difficulties sleeping at night. This often occurs in the moderate to severe stages of dementia, and may be challenging for caregivers to manage.
When it’s Provided

- Monday to Friday, from 7pm (up to 12 hours duration)n
- Transport option with subsidy is available if requiredn
- Government subsidies for Singaporeans and Permanent Residents are available based on means testingn
eligibility: Caregivers of persons requiring mild to moderate assistance in Activities of Daily Living (ADL), or persons living with dementia displaying sundowning behaviour. Government subsidies available for Singaporeans and Permanent Residents, subject to means testing.

name: CREST - Community Resource Engagement and Support Team
summary: Community-based mental health and dementia support by AIC, offering outreach, psychotherapy, caregiver support, and coordinated care with GPs, polyclinics, and hospitals. Includes youth outreach, post-diagnostic dementia support, aftercare, and primary care integration.
description:
AIC’s Community Mental Health Programmes build an integrated network of support so people with mental health conditions and dementia—and their caregivers—can access help closer to home.

Key components include:
- Community Outreach Teams (CREST) as a first-stop in the community to listen, identify needs early, and provide basic therapeutic support and linkage to services.
- Youth Community Outreach Teams (CREST-Youth) to raise awareness, identify youth mental health needs early, provide emotional support, involve caregivers, and connect families to health and social supports.
- Caregiver-focused outreach (CREST-CSN) to support caregivers at risk of depression, anxiety, or burnout through awareness, early identification of needs, and linkage to help.
- Community Intervention Teams (COMIT) offering psychotherapy and psychosocial interventions (e.g., cognitive behavioural therapy, psychoeducation) for persons with mental health issues or dementia and their caregivers, coordinated with GPs, polyclinics, and hospitals.
- Post-Diagnostic Support (CREST-PDS) for newly diagnosed persons living with dementia and their caregivers, providing education, coordinated resources, and early care planning for six months from referral.
- Aftercare transitional support to facilitate discharge from hospital, support adherence to care, reduce relapse, and reintegrate individuals with complex medical and social needs back into the community.
- Assessment & Shared Care Team (ASCAT) providing clinical consultation for primary care and community partners, triage by psychiatrists for urgent/severe cases, and gatekeeping fast-track access to hospital services.
- Mental Health in Primary Care to enable mild to moderate mental and chronic health conditions to be managed holistically by nearby GPs and polyclinics in less stigmatising settings.

These programmes aim to promote early identification, integrate health and social care, and strengthen a dementia care network so individuals and caregivers can be well supported where they live.
eligibility: Open to individuals in the community with mental health issues or dementia, and their caregivers. Youth experiencing psychological distress can receive support via CREST-Youth. Newly diagnosed persons living with dementia and their caregivers may receive post-diagnostic support (for six months from referral). Urgent/severe cases surfaced by GP partners and COMIT may be triaged by ASCAT psychiatrists for fast-track hospital services. Specific clinical suitability and referrals may be required depending on the programme.

- Community outreach (CREST): Raises awareness of dementia and mental health, promotes early detection, provides emotional support, conducts preventive and cognitive-stimulating activities, and links people to suitable health and social care services.

name: Senior Care Centres
summary: PCS Senior Care Centres offer full-day care programmes for seniors aged 60 and above, focusing on mental and physical well-being, social interaction, and support for caregivers. They provide meals, transport options, and a secure environment to promote dignified ageing in place.
description: PCS Senior Care Centres (SSC) provide full-day care programmes for Singaporeans and Permanent Residents aged 60 and above, aiming to promote ageing in place. The centres offer a secure environment with activities designed to enhance memory, social interaction, music engagement, and maintenance of daily living activities. Using the PCS MDC Individualised Care Plan, the centres provide maintenance exercises and regimental activities to stimulate mental and physical health, helping to prevent or delay cognitive decline. The centres also support frail and/or physically disabled seniors, improve their general well-being, and provide respite and support to their families and caregivers. Meals and transport (with additional charges) are provided at various locations operating Monday to Friday, with some centres open on Saturdays.
eligibility: Singaporeans and Permanent Residents aged 60 years and above.
whatItGives: Financial assistance for daily living expenses

name: Seniors Drop-In
summary: Drop-in social programme for King George’s Avenue seniors.
description: We aim to hinder the trend of senior isolation in Singapore by reaching out to the seniors living in King George’s Avenue. Our seniors drop-in programme provides a platform for these seniors to socialise with other seniors in the area to form closer relationships with their neighbours.
eligibility: Seniors living in King George’s Avenue.

name: Sheltered Workshop Programme
summary: Bizlink provides vocational training and work therapy programmes for Persons with Disabilities to develop skills and prepare them for employment, alongside caregiver support and vocational assessments.
description: Bizlink Centre Singapore Ltd offers a range of programmes designed to support Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) through vocational training, work therapy, day care activities, and employability support. Their services include sheltered workshop programmes, hydroponics work therapy, vocational assessments, and caregiver support, all aimed at developing work and social skills, promoting independence, and facilitating gradual transition into employment within a supportive environment.
eligibility: Applicants must be Persons with Disabilities, including physical, intellectual, developmental, hearing, or visual impairments, aged 18 years and above. Some programmes require basic work capability or independence in activities of daily living. Permanent Residents must have at least one immediate family member who is a Singapore Citizen. Eligibility and suitability are assessed via vocational assessment.

agency: Society of Sheng Hong Welfare Services
summary: Sheng Hong Active Ageing Centre (CARE) @ Sennett provides Active Ageing activities, Day Rehabilitation, and Day Care & Dementia Day Care for seniors. It helps older adults stay healthy and socially connected while offering respite for caregivers.
description:
- Community-based eldercare at Sheng Hong Active Ageing Centre (CARE) @ Sennett supporting seniors' health, independence and social well-being
- Active Ageing Programmes: group activities and courses designed to promote social interaction, mental stimulation and physical wellness so seniors can stay engaged and independent
- Day Rehabilitation: therapy-led sessions to help regain or maintain strength, mobility and functional abilities, guided by trained staff and personalised exercises
- Day Care & Dementia Day Care: structured daytime supervision and activities tailored to individual cognitive, physical and emotional needs, providing a safe, stimulating environment and easing caregiving load for families
- Mission-driven, holistic approach intended to value, support and empower seniors with dignity, purpose and joy
eligibility: Seniors/older adults who would benefit from active ageing activities, day rehabilitation, or structured day care (including those living with dementia) and who require daytime supervision or support.

name: Special Needs Savings Scheme
summary: A non-profit trustee and care planning service that helps families and caregivers secure long-term support for persons with disabilities and special needs. It manages funds, guides care planning, and offers savings and sponsorship schemes.
description:
- Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC) is a non-profit service that helps families and caregivers plan for the long-term financial and care needs of persons with disabilities and special needs.
- It provides professional trustee services to hold, manage, and disburse funds prudently for beneficiaries' future needs, ensuring continuity of support even when caregivers are no longer able to provide care.
- SNTC offers care planning and guidance to caregivers, aligning disbursements with beneficiaries' daily living, education, healthcare, and other needs.
- It features complementary programmes such as the Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS) and sponsorship schemes (e.g., GOAL/GOAL+) that help reduce the cost burden of setting up and maintaining plans.
- The service is designed to give families peace of mind by safeguarding resources, promoting responsible management, and ensuring consistent support throughout the beneficiary’s life.
eligibility:
SNSS is open to all persons with disabilities who:
Attend or have attended a Special Education (SPED) school
Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:
Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment
Moderate visual impairment or worst in the better eye
Moderate hearing loss or worse in the better ear
Intellectual disability
Autism

Proof of disability must be provided using the Disability Verification Form (DVF) completed by a relevant registered Healthcare Professional.

name: Special Needs Trust Company
summary: Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC) provides trust and future care planning services for persons with disabilities and special needs, supporting caregivers with structured financial arrangements and case-managed care plans. It helps ensure continuity of care and responsible disbursement of funds for beneficiaries’ long-term needs.
description:
- Non-profit trust service dedicated to safeguarding the long-term welfare of persons with disabilities and special needs in Singapore
- Supports caregivers and families to plan for the future through professional care planning and trust administration
- Key offerings include:
  - Special Needs Trust: Setting up and managing trust accounts to provide structured, needs-based disbursements for beneficiaries with special needs
  - Special Needs Savings Scheme: Facilitates CPF nominations to provide regular payouts for the beneficiary’s care after the caregiver’s passing
  - Case management and care planning: Dedicated case managers work with caregivers to develop a comprehensive care plan that guides future support and fund disbursement
  - Education and guidance for caregivers on future care planning and how to coordinate services across community resources
- Aims to give peace of mind to caregivers by ensuring continuity of care and prudent use of funds for their loved ones

name: StrokeConnect
summary: StrokeConnect is a peer-led helpline by the Singapore National Stroke Association that provides emotional support, information, and referrals to stroke survivors and caregivers. Trained befrienders with lived experience guide callers to suitable SNSA programmes and community resources.
description:
- A helpline that connects stroke survivors and caregivers with trained peer befrienders who are themselves stroke survivors
- Provides survivor-to-survivor listening, understanding, and emotional support based on lived experience
- Helps callers understand available SNSA programmes and links them to the most suitable options
- Guides users to relevant community resources and the next steps in their recovery or caregiving journey
- Non-clinical, non-medical support; focuses on sharing experiences, practical guidance, and referrals
- Operating hours: Monday to Friday, 09:00–18:00
- Brochures available in English and Chinese
eligibility: Intended for stroke survivors and caregivers seeking non-clinical peer support, information, or guidance on recovery resources. Not a medical or clinical advice service.

name: The Compassionate Network
summary: Support for caregivers of people nearing end-of-life.
description: The Compassionate Network (TCN) is a charity in Singapore dedicated to supporting caregivers of patients with advanced illnesses.Established in July 2023, TCN is the first and only charity dedicated to supporting caregivers of patients with advanced illnesses using lay helpers to form circles of care, to oﬀer companionship, guidance, grief education and more – ensuring they are not alone in their journey. **What We Do** TCN hopes to create a compassionate community by rallying volunteers, corporates, and community partners to form circles of care around caregivers of people nearing life's end. We recognise that family caregivers are themselves care recipients too – they deserve attention and support as much as those they care for. By nurturing the wellbeing of caregivers, we honour their dignity in caring for their loved ones in life's final chapter. We tailor our support according to the different needs of the caregivers - some prefer to focus on their personal well-being while others request assistance with various caregiving activities. Beyond the caregiving period, TCN supports caregivers into their bereavement phase and facilitate their transitions to a physical world without their loved ones.
eligibility: Open to volunteers, corporates, and community partners interested in supporting caregivers of people nearing end-of-life. No specific eligibility criteria for caregivers mentioned.
